title: Professional Life
description: Talk about the working life you have had and the one you want: name what a career is made of (a clerk, the management, a profit, a deficit, a degree, training, an internship, a scholarship, a physician and a physician's assistant, a diplomat, a clinic, surgery, a check-up, stitches, competitive work, to earn) and the feelings work leaves behind (guilty, relieved, envious, proud, fond of, fed up with - always with, and with an -ing form after it as after every English preposition -, hooked on, worthwhile, self-sufficient), with the phrasal verbs of a life story (to pick somebody up, to look after somebody, to settle down, to set up a company, to drop out) and the place a pronoun takes inside them (pick her up, never pick up her, while look after never splits) and the word that looks like a word in your own language and is not one (a stage is not an internship); say what a habit used to be and is no longer with used to + the base verb, against would for a repeated past action, against the past simple of one dated event, against a present habit, and against the look-alike be used to + a noun or an -ing form; give the aim of an action with to + the base verb, with in order to and with so that + a clause whose modal follows the tense of the main verb, and tell an aim apart from a consequence; and look back at what was not done with should have and shouldn't have + the past participle, the form of regret, and its second value, the assumption about what has probably happened already — all read through a job profile, an interview and the first step of the career research project
